figs.name: io-link-master-device-3-wire-diagram
figs.alt: IO-Link system diagram with master ports, point to point sensors and M12 3 wire pins
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog showing an IO Link master linking each port to one sensor or actuator over a 3 wire M12 cable up to 20 m, and to the PLC over fieldbus.
figs.after_h2: How IO-Link Works: Master, Device and the 3-Wire Connection

figs.name: io-link-operating-mode-selection-flowchart
figs.alt: IO Link port operating modes flowchart for COM, SIO, DI and DO mode
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog showing how an IO Link master port runs COM mode for a smart device, or SIO, DI and DO modes for conventional sensors and actuators.
figs.after_h2: IO-Link Four Operating Modes: From Simple Digital to Full Smart Communication
figs.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 600" width="100%" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif">
<title>IO Link port operating mode selection flowchart COM SIO DI DO</title>
<rect width="800" height="600" fill="#ffffff"/>

<text x="400" y="183.15" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">IO Link capable</text>
<text x="400" y="206.15" font-size="19" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">device?</text>
<polyline points="230,188 140,188 140,256" fill="none" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="190" y="176" font-size="18" fill="#134e4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Yes</text>
<polyline points="570,188 660,188 660,256" fill="none" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="612" y="176" font-size="18" fill="#134e4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">No</text>
<rect x="20" y="260" width="250" height="100" rx="10" fill="#0f766e" stroke="#134e4a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="145.0" y="292.95" font-size="17" fill="#ffffff" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">IO Link (COM) mode</text>
<text x="145.0" y="315.95" font-size="17" fill="#ffffff" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">COM1 4.8, COM2 38.4,</text>
<text x="145.0" y="338.95" font-size="17" fill="#ffffff" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">COM3 230.4 kbps</text>
<line x1="145" y1="360" x2="145" y2="384" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>

<text x="145.0" y="423.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Master reads IODD</text>
<text x="145.0" y="446.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">exchanges process,</text>
<text x="145.0" y="469.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">service and device</text>
<text x="145.0" y="492.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">data plus events</text>
<polygon points="660,264.0 785.0,316 660,368.0 535.0,316" fill="#fef3c7" stroke="#1a2b4a" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="660" y="311.3" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Sensor or</text>
<text x="660" y="333.3" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">actuator?</text>
<polyline points="660,368 660,386 560,386 560,404" fill="none" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="585" y="380" font-size="17" fill="#134e4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="end">Sensor</text>
<polyline points="660,386 720,386 720,404" fill="none" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<text x="712" y="378" font-size="17" fill="#134e4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Actuator</text>
<rect x="440" y="408" width="200" height="108" rx="10" fill="#f0fdfa" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="540.0" y="433.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">SIO or DI mode</text>
<text x="540.0" y="456.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">C/Q works as a</text>
<text x="540.0" y="479.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">standard digital</text>
<text x="540.0" y="502.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">input</text>
<rect x="650" y="408" width="140" height="108" rx="10" fill="#f0fdfa" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="720.0" y="433.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">DO mode</text>
<text x="720.0" y="456.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">C/Q drives</text>
<text x="720.0" y="479.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">lamp, valve</text>
<text x="720.0" y="502.45" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">or actuator</text>
<text x="400" y="556" font-size="18" fill="#134e4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Old NPN or PNP sensors still work on an IO Link master port</text>
</svg>

figs.name: io-link-four-data-types-infographic
figs.alt: IO Link process data, service data, device data and events explained
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog listing the four IO Link data types: cyclic process data up to 32 bytes, service parameters, device identification and instant diagnostic events.
figs.after_h2: IO-Link Four Types of Data Transmitted
figs.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 540" width="100%" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif">
<title>Four types of IO Link data: process, service, device and events</title>
<rect width="800" height="540" fill="#ffffff"/>
<defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0 0L10 5L0 10z" fill="#1a2b4a"/></marker></defs>
<text x="400.0" y="34" font-size="24" fill="#134e4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Four Types of IO Link Data</text>
<rect x="25" y="62" width="365" height="200" rx="14" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#0f766e" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<rect x="25" y="62" width="365" height="52" rx="14" fill="#0f766e"/>
<rect x="25" y="100" width="365" height="14" fill="#0f766e"/>
<circle cx="57" cy="88" r="17" fill="#ffffff"/>
<text x="57" y="94" font-size="18" fill="#0f766e" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">1</text>
<text x="87" y="96" font-size="21" fill="#ffffff" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Process data</text>
<text x="47" y="154" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">measured value in digital form</text>
<text x="47" y="188" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">sent every cycle, no request</text>
<text x="47" y="222" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">up to 32 bytes, 400 µs at COM3</text>
<rect x="410" y="62" width="365" height="200" rx="14" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#0369a1" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<rect x="410" y="62" width="365" height="52" rx="14" fill="#0369a1"/>
<rect x="410" y="100" width="365" height="14" fill="#0369a1"/>
<circle cx="442" cy="88" r="17" fill="#ffffff"/>
<text x="442" y="94" font-size="18" fill="#0369a1" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">2</text>
<text x="472" y="96" font-size="21" fill="#ffffff" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Service data</text>
<text x="432" y="154" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">parameters read or written</text>
<text x="432" y="188" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">units, switch point, damping</text>
<text x="432" y="222" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">backup and restore after a swap</text>
<rect x="25" y="282" width="365" height="200" rx="14" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#7c3aed" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<rect x="25" y="282" width="365" height="52" rx="14" fill="#7c3aed"/>
<rect x="25" y="320" width="365" height="14" fill="#7c3aed"/>
<circle cx="57" cy="308" r="17" fill="#ffffff"/>
<text x="57" y="314" font-size="18" fill="#7c3aed" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">3</text>
<text x="87" y="316" font-size="21" fill="#ffffff" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Device data</text>
<text x="47" y="374" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">manufacturer and device name</text>
<text x="47" y="408" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">serial number, hardware and</text>
<text x="47" y="442" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">firmware version</text>
<rect x="410" y="282" width="365" height="200" rx="14" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#b45309" stroke-width="2.5"/>
<rect x="410" y="282" width="365" height="52" rx="14" fill="#b45309"/>
<rect x="410" y="320" width="365" height="14" fill="#b45309"/>
<circle cx="442" cy="308" r="17" fill="#ffffff"/>
<text x="442" y="314" font-size="18" fill="#b45309" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">4</text>
<text x="472" y="316" font-size="21" fill="#ffffff" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="start">Events</text>
<text x="432" y="374" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">sent at once when abnormal</text>
<text x="432" y="408" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">contamination, low supply,</text>
<text x="432" y="442" font-size="18" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="start">calibration overdue</text>
<text x="400" y="520" font-size="17" fill="#134e4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Process data every cycle, events at once</text>
</svg>
